project.name: Agent Wizardry
project.summary: A skill any coding agent can follow. The agent reads a repository and builds a wizard in that repository's language.

briefing.title: What this repository is
briefing.body: The skill is .agents/skills/agent-wizardry/SKILL.md, in the Agent Skills format. This wizard operates Agent Wizardry itself, and it is Python because this repository's tooling is Python. Install the skill into ~/.agents/skills before asking an agent to wizard a different project.

tasks.title: Run the catalog tests
tasks.summary: Run the unittest suite that locks the validator, the runner, and the example catalogs.

tasks.title: Validate the catalogs
tasks.summary: Check this repo's catalog and the example catalogs against the Agent Wizardry rules.

tasks.title: Run the test workflow on GitHub
tasks.summary: Start the Test workflow on the current repository through GitHub Actions.
tasks.details: Requires the gh CLI, authenticated to a remote that has .github/workflows/test.yml. This does not run tests on your machine. Use the local test task for that.
prerequisites: This repo has a GitHub remote

tasks.title: Install the skill for every project
tasks.summary: Symlink this skill into the personal skill directories read by Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Grok, and Codex.
tasks.details: The folder name stays agent-wizardry. Claude Code reads ~/.claude/skills. Copilot reads ~/.copilot/skills and ~/.agents/skills. Cursor reads ~/.cursor/skills and ~/.agents/skills. Grok reads ~/.grok/skills and ~/.agents/skills. Codex reads ~/.agents/skills. The commands are the Install section of README.md.
steps: From a clone of this repository, set src to "$PWD/.agents/skills/agent-wizardry".
For each of ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.copilot/skills, ~/.cursor/skills, and ~/.grok/skills, run mkdir -p on the directory and ln -sfn "$src" "$dir/agent-wizardry".
Restart the agent. In Claude Code, run /reload-skills if the skills directory was created during the session.
Open another project and ask the agent to build a wizard in that project's language.
